transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

The main reason I’m here is that I keep getting stuck on work that takes real sit-down mental effort. Things like monthly reports, or planning a multi-site health event—I know they matter, but I hit this wall and end up putting them off. It’s been causing enough trouble that I figured I should talk to someone.
Would you say you've struggled with this kind of difficulty focusing and starting effortful tasks since you were a kid, or is this something that's really only become a problem more recently?

No, it’s definitely not just recent. Even back in elementary school, teachers would tell my parents I was bright, but I was always daydreaming. I’d lose worksheets, forget to turn in homework—unless my mom checked my backpack every night, things just wouldn’t make it in.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or lacking interest in things you used to enjoy?
Not really, no. I mean, I get frustrated with myself when I’m behind on things, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been persistently sad or that I’ve lost interest in things.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a variety of things—like work, health, or everyday matters—and having a hard time controlling that worry, even when there's no immediate problem?

I don’t think so. I worry about work when I’m behind, but it’s usually tied to an actual deadline or something I dropped the ball on. I wouldn’t say I’m worrying all the time about lots of different things for no reason.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble sitting still, or find yourself acting impulsively—like interrupting others or making quick decisions without thinking them through?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think of myself as especially restless or impulsive. I might shift around in my chair sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m constantly fidgeting or interrupting people. That’s not the main issue I notice.
Do these attention and organization difficulties also cause problems for you outside of work—like at home, in relationships, or in other daily activities?

Yeah, it does. I’m still getting by overall, but it shows up outside work too. At home or with friends, I’ll miss things or leave stuff to the last minute, and then I’m apologizing because I dropped the ball. People have had to cover for me sometimes, and that’s embarrassing. It’s not like everything is falling apart, but it definitely causes problems.

Thinking back to your childhood, were you ever described as hyperactive—like being unable to stay seated, always on the go, or talking excessively—or was it mainly the daydreaming and forgetfulness that stood out?

It was mainly the daydreaming and forgetfulness, from what I remember. Even in elementary school, teachers would tell my parents I was bright, but I was always zoning out, losing worksheets, or forgetting to turn in homework. My mom had to check my backpack every night or things just wouldn’t get handed in.

No significant hyperactive-impulsive symptoms (fidgeting, interrupting, restlessness) are endorsed, consistent with a predominantly inattentive presentation of ADHD. Symptom onset before age 12, chronicity, and cross-situational impairment support ADHD diagnosis per DSM-5/ICD-10 criteria.
